title: Sean McVay backs Rams' special teams coach, hopes new kicker will rejuvenate unit | United States
text:
Rams coach Sean McVay is hopeful new kicker Blake Grupe will help steady a special teams unit that struggled mightily in the team's overtime loss to the Bills.
Rams coach Sean McVay is hopeful new kicker Blake Grupe will help steady a special teams unit that struggled mightily in the team’s overtime loss to the Bills.
McVay says he still has a lot of confidence in special teams coach Bubba Ventrone and that no changes are going to be made at the coaching level. McVay is confident David Quessenberry can be effective taking over a starting role at left tackle in the wake of Alaric Jackson’s one-game suspension. It was already going to be a short week, but Sean McVay navigated unexpected business that affected the start of preparation for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals.
“You’re always ready for inevitable things to come up,” the Rams coach said Thursday. “He says, ‘How’s that tube? ’” McVay recalled.
“I said, ‘What do you mean? ’NFL Week 6 picks: Panthers defeat Eagles; Packers beat Cowboys Sam Farmer makes his picks and score predictions for Week 6 of the NFL season, with the Rams defeating the Cardinals and the Chargers falling to 0-6. The Rams hope that Grupe can clean up the kicking game and relieve criticism of the Rams’ struggling special teams.
McVay said this week that he has “a lot of confidence” in special teams coordinator“You’re continuing to figure out some of our identity,” McVay said Thursday, adding, “I have seen the intentionality from the group that I’m looking for. ”Grupe was signed off the New York Jets practice squad. Last season, he was released by the New Orleans Saints in late November after he made only 18 of 26 field-goal attempts.
The Indianapolis Colts signed Grupe and he made all 11 of his attempts.
“For these last five weeks, I’ve been staying ready, been doing what I need to do to take advantage of an opportunity,” Grupe said. Rams’ Alaric Jackson has suspension reduced to one game The veteran left tackle punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after an overtime loss on Sunday and was originally give two-game suspension. Quessenberry, 36, is a ninth-year pro. But he has not started a game since 2023, when he played for the Minnesota Vikings.
But McVay said Quessenberry was a “consummate pro” who has played “a lot of meaningful snaps” in his career and worked with the Rams’ first-team offense when Jackson has been held out while managing blood-clot issues.
“This is kind of why I’m here, when things like this happen,” Quessenberry said. “So I’m ready to go. This is what I’ve worked for. I’ve played this position my whole life.
Go out there on Sunday and play ball. I’m fired up. ”This will be the first game without Jackson since last season’s late December game against the Atlanta Falcons. With D.J.

“It’s been a little bit of time since he’s played football,” McVay said. “But if he’s feeling good, expect him to be up for the game. “But not at the expense of putting him in a situation that, if he did have to play, wasn’t good for him. ” Offensive lineman Justin Dedich, who has been on injured reserve because of a hand injury, also is eligible to return.
But interior linemen such as guards Kevin Dotson and Steve Avila have remained physically sound.
“We’ll pray that we stay healthy,” McVay said, “but at some point we’ll start his clock and get him in there. ”Gary Klein covers the Los Angeles Rams for the Los Angeles Times.
